item.text: {"question_id":"5B.5","answer":"In 2023, the Tshisekedi government adopted or supported several formal transparency and anti-corruption measures, including stronger procurement and treasury procedures, extractive-asset oversight, CENAREF and anti-money-laundering institutional arrangements, mining-royalty and carbon-credit distribution rules, and renegotiation of the Sicomines agreement after an EITI study identified deviations from its infrastructure commitments and an undisclosed amendment (BATCH-0014-E002; BATCH-0019-E003; BATCH-0015-E010; BATCH-0024-E006; BATCH-0011-E007). EITI reporting also documented public debate, open-data publication, follow-up mechanisms, and a high implementation score, but beneficial-ownership disclosure remained incomplete and earlier local revenue distribution had not complied with the framework (BATCH-0029-E007; BATCH-0029-E008). These measures show formal institutional activity, not proven enforcement: the available record does not establish completed sanctions, recovery, audit cooperation, or effective remedy. Counterevidence indicates that anti-corruption laws were implemented ineffectively; phantom payments, opaque special accounts, illicit mineral trade involving officials, and slow justice for politically exposed persons persisted (BATCH-0011-E013; BATCH-0028-E001). The 2023 gas auction involved documentary irregularities and an apparently altered evaluation that favored an ineligible bidder, although ministerial intervention was denied and no final investigation was reported (BATCH-0009-E007; BATCH-0009-E008). Parliamentary review later identified budget overruns, uncertified debts, emergency procedures, noncompliance with public-finance rules, and works lacking visible field action (BATCH-0024-E003; BATCH-0024-E004). Mining-related evictions, inadequate compensation, and lack of effective grievance or remedy mechanisms further indicate weak protection against state-linked or politically connected interests (BATCH-0010-E018). Overall, the evidence supports partial formal reform alongside weak, uneven, and incompletely attributed enforcement; it does not show that Tshisekedi personally ordered or benefited from the alleged
